newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA HAS NOT YET SET IRAQI OIL PURCHASE VOLUMES.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA HAS NOT YET SET IRAQI OIL PURCHASE VOLUMES.

text.p: Russia has not yet agreed, even in principle, the amount of Iraqi oil it will lift once Baghdad resumes oil exports under the second leg of the U.N. oil-for-food deal, a Russian energy official said on Thursday.

"It's too early to say what the volumes will be -- they will be made precise only as a result of negotiations," said Yuri Agababov, deputy general director of Zarubezhneft, the Russian trading company coordinating all Russian purchases of Iraqi oil.
He said oil and trading companies would fly to Baghdad to negotiate contracts, probably next week, but only after a pricing plan was approved by the United Nations.
When asked if Russia would contract for more or for less than it had lifted under the first, $2 billion leg of the programme, Agababov said, "Nobody right now can say."
He had said in June that Russia, a close ally of Iraq, was aiming to at least equal the amount it lifted under the first deal.
Eight Russian companies bought nearly 28.54 million barrels of oil under the first 180-day programme, or 23.5 percent of the total Baghdad was allowed to export under the first deal.
New Russian companies are known to want a slice of the action this time around.
Iraq is a step closer to resuming oil sales after U.N. oil experts sent Baghdad's new pricing plan on Wednesday to a Security Council panel, which has until Friday to approve or reject it.
If the pricing plan is approved, Iraq can sign individual oil contracts, which must be be endorsed by the U.N. oil experts or overseers, usually within 24 hours.

The oil-for-food programme allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food, medicine and other goods for its people to ease the effects of U.N. sanctions imposed seven years ago when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait.
